reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every pair of natural numbers d and n, given 3 ≤ n and n ≤ d, for every real κ with 4 ≤ κ, and for every real b with b = 1 or b = −1, make the following definitions. The quantifier order in the displayed statement is d, n, the two dimension hypotheses, κ, its lower-bound hypothesis, b, and its sign hypothesis. There are no existentially quantified parameters.

Put q = d div n and r = d mod n. Thus d = qn + r, q ≥ 1, and 0 ≤ r < n. Write E_m = ℝ^m with coordinates indexed by Fin m = {0,…,m−1}, its Euclidean structure, and its usual Borel σ-algebra. The real d-by-d matrix space also carries its Borel σ-algebra. All finite function spaces and products below carry their usual product Borel structures.

Let O(n) be the full real orthogonal matrix group, containing both determinant signs, and let H_n be its Haar measure normalized to have mass one on the entire compact group. Define the finite measure ν on O(n) by
    ν(S) = 2 H_n(S ∩ {O ∈ O(n) : det O = b})
for measurable S. This is restriction to the determinant-b set followed by multiplication by the real nonnegative-infinite scalar 2; the definition is not an additional sampling hypothesis.

For O ∈ O(n), define the real n-by-n matrix
    B(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) I_n − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
For a family (O_j)_{j∈Fin q}, define A(O_0,…,O_{q−1}) as the d-by-d block matrix whose first q consecutive blocks are B(O_0),…,B(O_{q−1}), each of size n, and whose final block is I_r. All entries between distinct blocks are zero. More explicitly, A_{jn+i,kn+ℓ} is B(O_j)_{iℓ} if j = k and is zero if j ≠ k, for j,k ∈ Fin q and i,ℓ ∈ Fin n; A_{qn+s,qn+t} = δ_{st} for s,t ∈ Fin r; and entries between the first qn coordinates and the final r coordinates are zero. This ordering is exactly the reindexing obtained from the bijection e : ((Fin n × Fin q) ⊕ Fin r) → Fin d with e(inl(i,j)) = jn+i and e(inr(s)) = qn+s.

Let D be the pushforward of the finite product measure ν^{⊗q} under the map (O_j)_j ↦ A(O_0,…,O_{q−1}). Thus D is a measure on the Borel space of all real d-by-d matrices.

Use G_m(C) to denote the total multivariateGaussian constructor with mean 0 ∈ E_m and matrix argument C: it is the pushforward of the standard Gaussian on E_m under z ↦ (CFC.sqrt C)z. Its covariance interpretation is C when C is positive semidefinite, and the approved definition specifies a point mass otherwise. All matrix inverses used here are the totalized matrix inverse, including at singular matrices. Define the measure-valued function γ on every real d-by-d matrix by
    γ(A) = G_d(A⁻¹).
Define the measure P on E_n and the measure μ on E_d by the measure integrals
    P = ∫_{O∈O(n)} G_n(B(O)⁻¹) ν(dO),
    μ = ∫_A γ(A) D(dA) = D.bind γ.
These integrals are the displayed Measure.bind constructions.

Define the coordinate splitting map
    split : E_d → (Fin q → E_n) × E_r
by
    split(x) = (((x_{jn+i})_{i∈Fin n})_{j∈Fin q}, (x_{qn+s})_{s∈Fin r}).
The WithLp conversions in the displayed definition preserve all these coordinate entries. The target has the finite function-space and product Borel structures and their usual default product norms; the assertion below is an equality of measures on this target.

Then all of the following hold, as a conjunction:
(1) D is a probability measure.
(2) For D-almost every real d-by-d matrix A, A is real symmetric positive definite.
(3) P is a probability measure.
(4) μ = D.bind γ is a probability measure.
(5) The pushforward of μ under split satisfies the exact measure identity
    split_* μ = P^{⊗q} ⊗ stdGaussian(E_r).
Here P^{⊗q} is the actual finite independent product of q copies of P, and the rightmost product is the binary product with the standard Gaussian on E_r. Equivalently, under this pushforward law, the q displayed n-coordinate blocks have the independent common law P, and their joint law is independent of the final r-coordinate standard Gaussian. The positivity assertion has only the D-almost-everywhere scope stated in (2); on that set γ(A) has the usual centered Gaussian interpretation with covariance A⁻¹.

The lower endpoints n = 3 and κ = 4 are allowed, as is d = n. A zero remainder r = 0 is allowed: E_0 contains only its zero vector and stdGaussian(E_0) is the probability point mass at that vector. There is no upper bound on κ and no restriction on the remainder beyond natural division. The same b and κ are used for every block. No unspecified constant, asymptotic estimate, additional dimension hypothesis, metric identity, or pointwise-in-A positivity conclusion occurs in the proposition.
